reason: The hypothesis synthesizes the known problem of Cu-rich grain boundary embrittlement in FeNiCrCoCu (P15) with the known high-temperature wear benefit of Mo in a different alloy system (CoCr matrix, P20/P24/P27) by proposing a specific mechanistic link—Mo segregation raising Cu diffusion barriers and enhancing boundary cohesion—that no passage states or suggests. It transfers the Mo effect to a new alloy and regime with a reasoned mechanism, and proposes a falsification test that would resolve whether this mechanism operates.

Mo improves high-temperature tribological performance in CoCr matrix alloys (P20, P24, P27)
Mo forms high-temperature solid lubricants (P24, P27)
